questions.questionText:
An airline needs people and equipment. These can be divided into factors of production.
What is allocated to its correct factor of production?
people or equipment factor of production

A government decides to move towards a market economy by selling state-owned enterprises.
What is a possible motive for this?

options.text: to extend government control of the economy
to take account of external costs

questions.questionText: Which factor can influence the price elasticity of supply of a product?

options.text: the degree of necessity of the product
the level of spare capacity in the industry
the proportion of income spent on the product

questions.questionText: What is a possible consequence of market failure?

options.text: Consumers have complete information about goods.
Some goods are no longer demanded.

questions.questionText:
Which organisations can directly fund the growth of firms?
central commercial
governments
banks banks

Which advantage do coins have that makes them more suitable than paper banknotes to act as
money?
Which statement about different income groups is correct?

options.text: High-income groups do not need to borrow money.
High-income groups save less money than low-income groups.
Low-income groups find it easier to borrow than high-income groups.
Low-income groups save a smaller percentage of their income than high-income groups.

questions.questionText:
A musician has a choice of playing for an orchestra in either Germany or England.
Which combination of incomes and cost of living is most likely to cause her to choose the
German orchestra?
incomes and cost of living in Germany compared with those in England
pre-tax (gross) income after-tax (net) income cost of living

A trade union states that its members have experienced a loss in real income over the past five
years.
What must have happened for this to be true?

options.text: Wages adjusted for inflation have fallen.

questions.questionText:
A firm provides a personal service to its customers. It prefers to remain labour-intensive rather
than changing to more capital-intensive production.
Which aspect of remaining labour-intensive would support this choice?

options.text: Quality of customer service is worse.

questions.questionText: Why might one profitable oil-drilling firm wish to take over another profitable oil-drilling firm?

options.text: to bring its suppliers into the same firm
to get closer to its customers to increase sales
to reduce its costs per unit of output
to reduce the amount of corporation tax it paid

questions.questionText:
A government decides to boost the economy through the use of a budget deficit.
Which target should it adopt to achieve this aim?

options.text: Direct taxation should exceed indirect taxation.
Export earnings should exceed import expenditure.
Government savings should exceed government investment.
Government spending should exceed government revenue.

questions.questionText:
A government decides to use a fiscal policy measure.
What is an example of this?

options.text: reducing the power of trade unions
reducing the rate of corporation tax

questions.questionText: What would the government reduce to decrease inflation?

A country wishes to encourage economic growth.
Which policy measure is most likely to achieve this aim?

options.text: reducing the maximum permitted hours of work

questions.questionText: How does a country usually measure its Gross Domestic Product?

options.text: by calculating the total value of all goods and services produced within the economy
by measuring the average prices of a basket of goods and services throughout the country
by subtracting government expenditure from government revenue
by surveying the number of people who are out of work but willing and able to work

questions.questionText: What is the most likely consequence of increased unemployment?
Why is deflation undesirable for an economy?
Why does a government provide public goods?

options.text: Public goods are always used by everyone.
Public goods are not profitable for private firms.
Public goods can only be provided by monopolies.
Public goods create large external costs.

questions.questionText:
The table shows the percentage changes in earnings and consumer prices for four countries in
one year.
Which country is likely to have experienced the greatest increase in real income during the year?
country earnings consumer prices

Which combination of government actions is most likely to raise the living standards of lower
income groups in an economy?
spending on personal tax-free
indirect tax
healthcare allowance
What is the usual effect of net immigration for a high-income country?

options.text: an increase in the size of the labour force
a rise in the average age of the population

Vietnamese companies buy insurance from companies in the US.
How will this transaction be recorded in the Vietnamese balance of payments?
section credit/debit

Country X produces cars and also imports cars.
Which group is least likely to benefit from the introduction of an import tariff on cars?

options.text: consumers of cars in country X
producers of cars in country X
workers making cars in country X

questions.questionText: What may be a cost to its home country when a multinational company (MNC) expands abroad?

options.text: Increased competition from the MNC may force firms in the host country to close.
Many jobs created by the MNC may be low-skilled.
The MNC’s profits from the host country may be sent to its home country.

The MNC may cause job losses in its home country by moving production abroad.
